messages.subject: Help with Bar Plot
parts:
Hello All,

Trying to learn ggplot2 and unable to figure out how to set the fill
color parameter.

My data is:

> dput(d1)
structure(list(Name = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"), Value =
c(-47.6811594202899,
-20.5357142857143, 53.1707317073171, -52.2222222222222,
59.7402597402597,
-35.2040816326531, 171.954545454545)), .Names = c("Name", "Value"
), row.names = c(2L, 3L, 4L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 11L), class = "data.frame")


p <- ggplot(d1, aes( substr(Name,1,15), Value, fill = Value))
p <- p + opts(panel.border = theme_blank())
theme_set(theme_bw()) #To remove background
p <- p + geom_bar(aes(fill = Value)) + theme_bw()
p

I want to fill the colors with "green" (+ve) and "red"(-ve) the
intensity of the color based on the value.

I am not sure which parameters I need to set.

Please help!

Thank you.

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Help with Bar Plot
parts:
scale_fill_gradient2()

ggplot(d1, aes(substr(Name,1,15), Value, fill = Value))+ opts(panel.border = theme_blank())+ geom_bar()+ scale_fill_gradient2(low="red", high="green")

It centers the colors at 0 so red isn't very red because in your dataset the numbers <0 aren't of the same magnitude as the >0 numbers. 

B

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Help with Bar Plot
parts:
I thought you wanted the the intensity to map to the distance from 0? 

Without gradient you will have to define your colors manually. Just doesn't seem worth the effort unless this is for something very special. 

If you're going to use manual scaling, just remember that the color of the bars is a "fill" and not a "color" or "colour". In other words, scale_fill_manual(). 

B

messages.subject: Re: Help with Bar Plot
parts:
I think if you want to make them discrete you'd be better off creating a new column in your dataframe that is color.factor or something. 

something like


d1$col.factor<-NA
d1[d1$Value < 0,]$col.factor<-"R"
d1[d1$Value >= 0,]$col.factor<-"G"

ggplot(d1, aes(x=substr(Name,1,15), y=Value, fill = col.factor))+
geom_bar()+
theme_bw()+
opts(panel.border = theme_blank())+
scale_fill_manual(values=c("R"="red", "G"="green"))


HTH,

B

parts:
Red-green contrasts are a bad idea because 5-10% of men have a
red-green colour weakness that will make the plot difficult to read.

Hadley
